newsitem.title: GERMANY: Freight forwarding industry urged to plan for Euro.
newsitem.headline: Freight forwarding industry urged to plan for Euro.

text.p: European freight forwarders need to start planning for the Euro as soon as possible to be ready for European currency union in 1999, senior industry figures said.
Manfred Boes, president of the German freight forwarders association BSL, said forwarders should start planning now because the Euro would come despite open questions of when and how.

Speaking at a conference on European currency union and the forwarding industry, he said forwarders needed to analyse how the Euro would affect business regardless of whether they operated only nationally or internationally.

"How quickly forwarders will be confronted with the Euro change-over will depend considerably on their client structure. As forwarders, we will probably be confronted with the very different wishes and demands of our customers more quickly than we think," he said.
Walter Stork, chairman of sea freight forwarder Navis AG, called on German freight forwarders to switch rates quickly to Euros in 1999 or face losing business to rivals from neighbouring countries.

"It makes sense immediately after the introduction of the Euro to offer through transport exclusively in Euros. Whoever has the courage to do that can expect considerable competitive advantages," he said.
Clients in non-Euro countries, and in particular overseas, could pressure for U.S. dollar invoicing and forwarders would need to convince them of the advantages of the Euro, he stated.
Large shippers already obtain quotes from forwarders in different countries so a single currency would not bring additional price transparency, he said.
Navis itself expected currency change-over costs of 100,000 marks on turnover of 100 million marks which was a far lower figure than some estimates of up to two percent of turnover, he noted.
